domain_restrictions: The product index i ranges over integers i = 1,2,...,r; when r = 0 the product is empty and equals 1

Implicitly, the denominator factors (1 - q^i) for i = 1,...,r must be meaningful (nonzero) if q is a numeric parameter; alternatively the identity is intended in a formal/polynomial/rational-function sense where the expression is well-defined
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the quantity defined by [n choose r]_q := (∏_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)))/(∏_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)), with ∏_{i=1}^0 := 1, satisfies [n choose r]_q = [n choose (n-r)]_q, where [n choose (n-r)]_q is defined by the same formula with r replaced by (n-r).
quantifier_order: with 0 <= r <= n: define [n choose r]_q by the given product (empty product convention when r = 0); then assert equality [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q

statement_nl: For integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.
